text:
Running a production database on a 2 GB VPS sounds like a bad idea, but it's also been some of the most fun we've had with Postgres. This post is about getting real performance out of very small hardware.

We started out optimistic and set `shared_buffers` to 512 MB, because a big cache seemed like an obvious win. Three OOM kills in the first month changed our minds. The Linux kernel doesn't negotiate. Your memory budget has to cover every connection and worker, plus the background processes.

PgBouncer made the biggest difference. Connection pooling cut our active connections from 200 to 20. Latency dropped, and the little VPS started punching well above its weight.

Below are the mistakes we made and the tuning that eventually turned a shaky setup into a stable one.
